item.title: Optimizing Document Lookup: Making Atlas Search and Vector Search Up to 5x Faster
item.description:
元記事公開：2026/11/11 9:00:00（日本時間）
Sometimes the biggest performance gains come not from making core operations faster, but from eliminating unnecessary work surrounding them. That is exactly what we discovered while optimizing document lookup in MongoDB Atlas Search and Vector Search. By removing redundant query planning and execution overhead, we made search queries up to 5x faster without changing the underlying search algorithms.

item.title: Introducing MongoDB Atlas Sharding Advisor: Know When and How to Scale Sharded Clusters
item.description:
元記事公開：2026/11/2 9:00:00（日本時間）
As applications grow, database teams need to make increasingly complex decisions about how to distribute data, manage workloads, and scale their infrastructure. Sharding enables MongoDB to scale horizontally, but managing a sharded cluster can introduce its own challenges. Understanding cluster health, diagnosing uneven load, and choosing an appropriate shard key can require piecing together metrics across multiple views and relying on specialized expertise.

item.title: MongoDB Extension for Hibernate ORM is Now GA
item.description:
元記事公開：2026/10/13 9:00:00（日本時間）
The MongoDB Extension for Hibernate ORM is now generally available, giving Java teams a production-ready way to use familiar Hibernate APIs with MongoDB’s document model. It is a first-party, open-source library that enables Java applications to use MongoDB as the backing database via the Hibernate ORM. The extension allows Java developers to enjoy the same experience with MongoDB, reducing the friction for those who want to switch.

item.title: Same Query, Same Score: Consistent Ranking with StableTfl in Atlas Search
item.description:
元記事公開：2026/9/25 9:00:00（日本時間）

Page one ends with "Flourless Chocolate Cake." They click next, and the first result on page two is "Flourless Chocolate Cake" again. Between the two requests, nothing about the query changed; only the requested page did. An Atlas Search customer running paginated search brought us this exact problem.
